Question 1
?

Let p=⟨1,−1,1⟩ and q=⟨8,4,2⟩. Find the vector projection of q onto p.

a
⟨−13,−13,13⟩
b
⟨2,−2,2⟩
c
⟨6,−6,6⟩
d
⟨63,63,63⟩
e
⟨3,−3,−3⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The projection is proj_p(q) = ((q·p)/(p·p))p. Since q·p = 8−4+2 = 6 and p·p = 3, the projection is 2p = ⟨2,−2,2⟩.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Let $p=⟨1,-1,1⟩$ and $q=⟨8,4,2⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p.$
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & =\frac{p\cdot q}{p\cdot p}p \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{{p}_{x}^{2}+{p}_{y}^{2}+{p}_{z}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 8+(-1)\cdot 4+1\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{6}{3}⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components
content.problem: Let $p=⟨1,-1,1⟩$ and $q=⟨8,4,2⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $q$ onto $p.$
content.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{p}\,q & =\frac{p\cdot q}{p\cdot p}p \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{{p}_{x}^{2}+{p}_{y}^{2}+{p}_{z}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 8+(-1)\cdot 4+1\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}p \\  & =\frac{6}{3}⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Let $a=⟨2,-1,-2⟩$ and $b=⟨x,-4,0⟩.$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =2\cdot x+(-1)\cdot (-4)+(-2)\cdot 0 \\  & =2x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2x+4 & =0 \\ 2x & =-4 \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
